evals.query: Set up a Kora SOAP client in Java from a WSDL in src/main/resources/wsdl for an external CustomerService. Give me the Gradle build file and the application graph.
expected_behavior: Applies the com.github.bjornvester.wsdl2java Gradle plugin and sets wsdlDir, packageName, generatedSourceDir and useJakarta = true
Uses platform("io.koraframework:kora-bom:$koraVersion") with koraVersion=2.0.0.RC2 from plain mavenCentral(), and never pins an individual io.koraframework artifact version
Declares annotationProcessor "io.koraframework:annotation-processors" and implementation "io.koraframework:soap-client"
Adds an HTTP transport module (http-client-ok / http-client-apache / http-client-jdk) and a config module, and notes the generated client needs an HttpClient component
Extends the @KoraApp interface with io.koraframework.soap.client.common.SoapClientModule plus the transport and config modules
Explains the two-stage chain: wsdl2java -> jakarta.jws @WebService interface -> Kora processor -> $CustomerService_SoapClientImpl and @Module $CustomerService_SoapClientModule
States that the generated $CustomerService_SoapClientModule is picked up automatically and must not be extended from @KoraApp
Sets a Java 25 toolchain
anti_behavior: Writes ru.tinkoff.kora:kora-parent, ru.tinkoff.kora:soap-client or any ru.tinkoff.kora coordinate
Adds annotationProcessor "io.koraframework:soap-client-annotation-processor" separately as if annotation-processors did not already contain it
Adds exclude group: "jakarta.xml" / "org.glassfish.jaxb" / "com.sun.activation" blocks to the soap-client dependency
Sets useJakarta = false or omits it
Adds Apache CXF as a runtime dependency, or a Spring-WS / JAX-WS RI runtime
Adds the generated $CustomerService_SoapClientModule to the @KoraApp extends list

evals.query: Same thing but in Kotlin with KSP: wsdl2java generates the interface but Kora generates no client for it. What is my build.gradle.kts missing?
expected_behavior: Identifies that wsdl2java emits Java sources and KSP only sees them when the generated directory is on the Java source set
Adds sourceSets.main { java.srcDir(layout.buildDirectory.dir("generated/sources/wsdl2java/java")) }
Uses ksp("io.koraframework:symbol-processors:...") with the kora-bom platform, Kotlin 2.4.20 and KSP 2.3.12
Keeps useJakarta.set(true)
Suggests ./gradlew kspKotlin --console=plain to see the processor diagnostics
Keeps the Java @WebService interface as the contract instead of re-declaring it in Kotlin
anti_behavior: Suggests kapt, or adds the annotation processor via annotationProcessor in a KSP project
Adds kotlinx-coroutines to make the client work
Rewrites the CXF-generated interface by hand in Kotlin
Pins Kotlin 1.9.x or the 1.9-based KSP plugin

evals.query: How do I call the generated Kora SOAP client SimpleService from my own @Component, and where does its configuration live?
expected_behavior: Injects the @WebService interface SimpleService by constructor into a @Component
Calls the operation method directly and uses the returned WSDL payload type, e.g. TestResponse response = service.test(request)
Configures soapClient.SimpleService.url (required) and optionally timeout (default 60s)
States that the config section name comes from @WebService.name, which is the WSDL portType name, falling back to serviceName, portName, then the interface simple name
Mentions that SoapServiceConfig is registered tagged with @Tag(SimpleService.class)
Notes that Kotlin sees the Java contract as platform types, so payload fields should be treated as nullable
anti_behavior: Injects $SimpleService_SoapClientImpl or casts the injected interface to it for normal calls
Claims the method returns a SoapResult, a wrapper or a future
Uses the wsdl:service name (e.g. SimpleServiceService) as the config section
Constructs the client manually with new when the generated component already exists
Uses field injection

evals.query: I need a non-blocking SOAP call in Kora. Give me a suspend fun in Kotlin, or a Mono/CompletionStage in Java, for my SimpleService client.
expected_behavior: States that Kora 2.0 contracts are synchronous and run on virtual threads, and that the generated SOAP client only overrides the WSDL interface's own synchronous methods
States that the 1.x <method>Async returning CompletionStage on $Iface_SoapClientImpl was removed in 2.0
Confirms there is no *Reactive, Mono, Flux, CompletionStage or suspend SOAP variant generated by either the annotation processor or KSP
Warns against enabling wsdl2java async method generation, because the generated mapping casts the SOAP body straight to the declared return type
Offers concurrency at the caller instead (virtual threads / structured concurrency), not a fake async client API
anti_behavior: Shows testReactive(request) returning Mono<T>
Shows casting to $SimpleService_SoapClientImpl to reach a testAsync method
Declares suspend fun test(...) on the SOAP interface or a Kotlin wrapper implementing it
Adds reactor-core, kotlinx-coroutines or http-client-async to make the call non-blocking
Invents a Kora annotation to make the method asynchronous

evals.query: My WSDL-generated interface uses javax.jws.WebService and javax.xml.ws.Holder. The build succeeds but Kora never generates a client. Why?
expected_behavior: Identifies that the Kora 2.0 processors only handle jakarta.jws.WebService and register no javax variant, so a javax interface is silently skipped
Fixes it at the source: set useJakarta = true in the wsdl2java block and regenerate
Requires a clean rebuild so the previously generated javax sources do not linger in the source set
Confirms the correct imports are jakarta.jws.WebService, jakarta.jws.WebMethod, jakarta.xml.ws.Holder, jakarta.xml.bind.*
Explains the absence of any error message: the processor matches on the annotation, so a non-matching interface produces neither output nor a diagnostic
anti_behavior: Adds a javax-to-jakarta shim, a bytecode transformer or javax.jws dependencies
Claims Kora 2.0 supports both javax.jws and jakarta.jws as 1.x did
Hand-edits the generated interface's imports instead of fixing the generator setting
Suggests writing the @WebService interface manually to work around it

evals.query: Migrate this Kora 1.x SOAP build file to 2.0: koraBom platform("ru.tinkoff.kora:kora-parent:1.2.16"); annotationProcessor "ru.tinkoff.kora:annotation-processors"; annotationProcessor "ru.tinkoff.kora:soap-client-annotation-processor"; implementation "ru.tinkoff.kora:json-module"; implementation("ru.tinkoff.kora:soap-client") { exclude group: "jakarta.xml"; exclude group: "org.glassfish.jaxb"; exclude group: "com.sun.activation" }
expected_behavior: Replaces the BOM with platform("io.koraframework:kora-bom:$koraVersion") at koraVersion=2.0.0.RC2
Keeps only annotationProcessor "io.koraframework:annotation-processors" and drops the separate soap-client-annotation-processor, which that artifact already aggregates

Replaces implementation "io.koraframework:soap-client" without any exclude block, explaining that 2.0 soap-client declares jakarta.xml.ws-api, jakarta.xml.bind-api and org.glassfish.jaxb:jaxb-runtime as api dependencies on purpose
Maps ru.tinkoff.kora:json-module to io.koraframework:json-common, and notes SOAP itself does not need it
Raises the toolchain to Java 25
Notes that a package rename requires ./gradlew clean --continue then classes testClasses --no-build-cache
anti_behavior: Keeps the jakarta / glassfish / com.sun.activation exclude blocks
Emits io.koraframework:kora-parent or io.koraframework:json-module, neither of which exists
Pins a version on an individual io.koraframework artifact instead of relying on the BOM
Pins 2.0.0-SNAPSHOT or 2.0.0.alpha6 for a normal project
Adds a snapshot repository when mavenCentral() suffices for 2.0.0.RC2

evals.query: This 1.x SOAP config stopped working after upgrading to Kora 2.0 — SOAP metrics disappeared and my payload logging is gone: soapClient { SimpleServiceService { url = ... , timeout = 30s } } and logging.level { "com.example.generated.soap.SimpleService" = "DEBUG" }
expected_behavior: Points out that the section name must be the @WebService name (the WSDL portType, SimpleService), not the wsdl:service name SimpleServiceService, and that the wrong section leaves url unset so the graph fails on a null config value
Points out that telemetry.metrics.enabled defaults to false in Kora 2.0 (it was true in 1.x) and must be set explicitly per client
Renames logging.level to logging.levels
States that envelope bodies are only logged at TRACE, on the loggers <interface FQN>.request and <interface FQN>.response
Notes telemetry.logging.enabled must also be true for those loggers to exist at all
Lists the only valid keys: url, timeout, telemetry.logging.enabled, telemetry.metrics.enabled/slo/tags, telemetry.tracing.enabled/attributes
anti_behavior: Invents soapClient.<Service> keys such as headers, retries, connectTimeout, keepAlive or maxConnections
Claims an unknown HOCON key produces a warning or an error
Says metrics are enabled by default in 2.0
Keeps logging.level
Tells the user to raise io.koraframework.soap to TRACE to get the payloads

evals.query: After renaming my packages to io.koraframework the build fails with hundreds of 'package ru.tinkoff.kora.example.generated.soap does not exist' errors, all in files under build/generated/sources/wsdl2java. Can I just fix the imports in those files?
expected_behavior: Says no — generated sources must never be edited, the edits are wiped on the next generation and hide the real cause
Explains the cause: wsdl2java does not delete its previous output and the build-cache key does not account for a changed packageName, so the old and new packages coexist in one source set
Gives the fix: ./gradlew clean --continue then ./gradlew classes testClasses --continue --no-build-cache
Confirms that after the clean rebuild no ru.tinkoff.kora reference should remain in compiler output, and that any remaining one is a real reference in sources or generator settings
Notes the same rule applies to other generators (OpenAPI, protobuf)
anti_behavior: Edits, sed-replaces or patches anything under build/generated
Adds a ru.tinkoff.kora dependency so the missing package resolves
Adds the old package to the source set or an exclude filter
Blames the Kora annotation processor for the errors

evals.query: How do I handle SOAP faults and transport failures from a Kora 2.0 SOAP client call, in Java and in Kotlin?
expected_behavior: Catches the generated @WebFault exception first for faults declared in the WSDL, reading its typed getFaultInfo()
Catches SoapFaultException for a fault whose detail matches no declared type, and reads e.getFault() returning SoapFault
Uses the real SoapFault accessors getFaultcode() (a QName), getFaultstring(), getFaultactor(), getDetail()
Uses SoapInvalidHttpResponseException for a status code other than 200 or 500
Uses SoapRequestMarshallingException / SoapResponseUnmarshallingException, noting that in 2.0 both extend SoapException
Explains that transport failures arrive as a SoapException wrapping HttpClientConnectionException or HttpClientTimeoutException
Imports everything from io.koraframework.soap.client.common.exception
anti_behavior: Uses InvalidHttpResponseSoapException (the 1.x name) instead of SoapInvalidHttpResponseException
Calls e.getSoapFault(), fault.getFaultCode() or fault.getFaultString() — none of which exist
Calls getStatusCode() or getResponseBody() on SoapInvalidHttpResponseException
Catches a bare java.net.ConnectException from the SOAP call
Invents SoapServiceException or a per-fault exception class not generated from the WSDL

evals.query: The SOAP service needs a WS-Security UsernameToken header on every request. How do I add it to my Kora SOAP client?
expected_behavior: Declares a component of type Function<SoapEnvelope, SoapEnvelope> annotated @Tag(SimpleService.class) in a @Module interface
Uses io.koraframework.soap.client.common.util.SoapEnvelopeProcessorsUtils.wssAuth(username, password)
Explains that the generated module injects this processor as an optional tagged dependency, so nothing else needs replacing
Notes that the password is sent as plaintext PasswordText, so the endpoint must be HTTPS, and sources the credentials from config rather than literals
Mentions that custom headers can be appended to envelope.getHeader().getAny()
Notes @Module interfaces are auto-discovered and must not also be extended from @KoraApp
anti_behavior: Uses SoapEnvelopeProcessors (the 1.x class name) instead of SoapEnvelopeProcessorsUtils
Uses @InterceptWith, which is the declarative HTTP client mechanism and does not apply to SOAP clients
Adds Apache CXF WSS4J interceptors or a runtime JAX-WS Handler chain
Sets an Authorization HTTP header instead of a SOAP header when the contract asks for WS-Security
Replaces the generated client component when the tagged processor would suffice

evals.query: My Kora build fails with 'No component found for dependency io.koraframework.soap.client.common.telemetry.SoapClientTelemetryFactory' and the SOAP client is missing from the graph. What is wrong?
expected_behavior: Adds io.koraframework.soap.client.common.SoapClientModule to the @KoraApp interface for the SoapClientTelemetryFactory error
Checks that an HTTP transport module is present, since the generated module requires an HttpClient component
Verifies the annotation processor is on the build: annotationProcessor "io.koraframework:annotation-processors" or ksp "io.koraframework:symbol-processors"
Verifies wsdl2java ran with useJakarta = true and that the interface really carries jakarta.jws.WebService
Runs ./gradlew clean classes so both generators run in order
Reminds that the injected type is the @WebService interface, not $Iface_SoapClientImpl
anti_behavior: Adds the generated $Iface_SoapClientModule to the @KoraApp extends list
Writes a @Component that implements the @WebService interface by hand
Disables annotation processing or adds a runtime reflection-based fallback
Adds ru.tinkoff.kora artifacts to satisfy the missing component

evals.query: Our Grafana dashboard for the SOAP client went blank after the Kora 2.0 upgrade. It queried kora_soap_client_requests_total with soap_service and status labels. What should it query now, and why is there no data?
expected_behavior: States that the SOAP client now reports a single Micrometer Timer named rpc.client.call.duration (RC1 called it rpc.client.duration)

Gives the real tags: rpc.system.name=soap, rpc.service, rpc.method, server.address, server.port, http.response.status_code, error.type, soap.fault.code, system.config, system.name.simple, system.name.canonical
Explains the blank dashboard has two causes: the metric was renamed, and telemetry.metrics.enabled now defaults to false
Notes that a MeterRegistry must be on the graph (MetricsModule from io.koraframework:micrometer-module) or metrics stay off regardless of the flag
Suggests alerting on error_type != "" or soap_fault_code != "" rather than a status label
Mentions the span name is SOAP <service> <method> with SpanKind.CLIENT
anti_behavior: Keeps kora.soap.client.requests / kora.soap.client.duration / kora.soap.client.faults
Uses soap_service, soap_method, status or fault_code as a 1.x-style tag set
Describes the duration metric as a DistributionSummary
Claims metrics are on by default
Invents a separate fault counter metric
